question: What is the potentially noisy elements of the dataset?
keywords: noise noisy quality errors artifacts outliers inaccuracies inconsistencies corrupted
summary: Describes potentially noisy elements of the dataset.
description:
Describes what kinds of noises a dataset might encompass.

The free-form text specifies fields or samples that might be noisy.

Alternatively, it can also be used to describe various noises that could impact the whole dataset.

retrieval.hypothetical_passage: The dataset has several known data-quality issues. Some questions used uncommon function signatures, edge-case inputs, or unusual patterns that may cause spurious model failures. We observed that the incorrect and correct solutions attached to problems are not guaranteed to compile or execute in the exact same way as in their original source. Some solutions will fail compilation or produce sandbox violations. The labels exhibit annotation disagreement; gold labels may be inaccurate. We observed inter-annotator disagreement rates and identified outliers. The corpus may contain duplicates that were not fully filtered. Users should be aware that the dataset contains noise from the source collection process.

extraction.instruction: Extract the noise, errors, or quality issues the source acknowledges in the dataset, including which fields, splits, or sample percentages they affect.
extraction.field_spec: SPDX property `dataset_datasetNoise`. Free-form text (xsd:string), 0..* values; each value names a noise source and the affected scope when stated.
extraction.output_guidance: Look for any acknowledgement of noise, label disagreement, annotation errors, mislabelled examples, duplicates, OCR errors, compilation failures, or other data-quality issues anywhere in the context. Statements about labels 'not being guaranteed correct', tests being 'flaky' or 'noisy', or known issues with subsets all count. Capture quantitative estimates (error rates, percentages) verbatim. Distinguish per-field noise from dataset-wide noise. Return noAssertion only when no quality caveat appears.
